title: sku-aware-prefill-curator-and-quant-safety-lattice
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces SKU-aware prefill curator (defaults + safety lattice) and a conservative quantization fallback policy. Adds telemetry to track per-tenant prefill hit-rate and unit-econ deltas. Backwards compatible; enabled behind tenant flag.
description:
Summary: Add a tenant/sku-aware prefill curator that selects conservative prefill + quantization defaults per-tenant and a safety lattice to gracefully fall back quant profiles if regeneration quality drops. Motivation: customers running Dedicated and Private deployments were seeing unit-econ regressions after blanket quant profile rollouts; ops needed a safer default that accounts for SKU (GPU type / reserved capacity) and workload characteristics. This PR implements a curator service that synthesizes a tenant-level default profile, records telemetry for unit economics, and provides a runtime safety lattice for quant fallbacks.

Design and motivation: The curator runs as part of the prefill decision path and emits small, deterministic profile objects that contain: sku_hint, batch_target_ms, warmup_prefill_factor, kv_cache_policy, quant_profile_hint, and safety_priority_score. The safety lattice is a lightweight policy graph evaluated at request-time: if generation quality (measured by token-level loss proxy and eval set pass rate) drops beyond thresholds, runtime will downgrade to a less aggressive quant profile and increase prefill/warmup. The intent is to minimize cost regressions while preserving throughput.

What changed (high level commits): - feat: core curator implementation and profile serializer - feat: runtime hook for safety-lattice evaluation (inference-serving) - chore: expose tenant flag, config map, and helm values for on-prem/private installs - test: unit tests for profile selection rules and safety transitions - perf: telemetry counters and tracing hooks for unit-econ deltas - docs: short runbook and README for operators

Commits (summary): - e9b4c6f: introduce prefill_curator service and profile model - d2a799b: add sku hint extraction from deployment metadata - 3f0a1bd: runtime hook: evaluate_safety_lattice() and apply_fallback() - 7c1a55e: instrumentation: prefills.prefill_hits, prefills.prefill_misses, econ.unit_cost_delta - 9b3f2ee: helm values + tenant feature flag - a12b77c: unit tests and integration skeleton - 5d4f001: fix lint and flake in prefill selection tests

Files touched (illustrative): - services/prefill/curator.py - services/prefill/profile_model.py - infra/helm/values-prefill.yaml - inference/runtime/safety_lattice.py - tests/unit/test_prefill_curator.py - docs/ops/prefill-curator-runbook.md - observability/metrics/prefill_metrics.yaml - examples/tenant-defaults/sample-tenant.yaml - ci/prefill-integration.yml

Small diffs (illustrative snippets included inline to aid reviewers): - infra/helm/values-prefill.yaml + enable_prefill_curator: true + prefill:
     default_profiles: {} +     sku_overrides: {} - services/prefill/profile_model.py + class PrefillProfile:
+    sku_hint: str
+    batch_target_ms: int
+    warmup_prefill_factor: float
+    quant_profile_hint: str
+    safety_priority_score: float

- inference/runtime/safety_lattice.py + def evaluate_safety_lattice(profile, metrics):
+    \"\"\"Return safe_profile or fallback_profile depending on recent quality telemetry\"\"\"
+    if metrics.quality_drop_pct > profile.safety_threshold:
+        return profile.less_aggressive_quant()
+    return profile

Backward compatibility and rollout: The feature is guarded by a tenant-level flag 'prefill_curator.enabled' and defaulted to off for legacy tenants. The helm chart exposes cluster-wide defaults and per-tenant overrides; Private installs can seed curated defaults via values-prefill.yaml. The runtime hook is additive and will only change behavior when the feature flag and tenant profile indicate a non-default configuration.

Telemetry & observability: Added metrics and traces to make regression debugging easier: - prefills.prefill_attempts (labels: tenant, sku, route) - prefills.prefill_hits, prefills.prefill_misses - econ.unit_cost_estimate and econ.unit_cost_delta (per-tenant rolling histogram) - tracing spans: prefill.curator.select and prefill.runtime.apply_fallback Runbook includes queries and dashboards for the above, and an alert recommendation for econ.unit_cost_delta > 15% sustained over 10m.

Tests and CI: Unit tests cover selection logic and a synthetic safety transition path. Integration job runs a short smoke test that verifies the runtime hook applies a fallback on contrived low-quality signals. Lint failed once due to typing on profile model; fixed in a followup commit. CI summary: unit-tests passed on linux, integration prefills passed on rerun, e2e telemetry flake reran and passed.

Review conversation (high level, chronological): - Arjun Patel (review): \"Nice focused change. Two questions: (1) can we avoid a sync call in the hot path when extracting sku metadata? (2) please add a conservative default for on-prem GPUs (A100-40GB) in the values file.\" - Maya (author reply): \"Good catches. I replaced the sync call with cached metadata and added sku_defaults for A100/RTX as requested. Also added a small opt-out checkbox in tenant defaults.\" - Sofia Martinez (request changes): \"Add a unit test for the fallback path where quality improves again (so we ensure we don't stay downgraded permanently). Also add metrics for fallback_count.\" - Maya: \"Added test and metric; updated description to clarify transient fallback semantics.\" - Leo Grayson (approve): \"Approach looks safe; feature flag and tenant opt-in make me comfortable.\" - CI bot: \"lint failed on first run; subsequent commits resolved issues.\"

Followups and known limitations: - We intentionally do not attempt automatic model-level eval comparisons inside the curator; that's out of scope. The curator consumes simple quality proxy metrics emitted by the runtime and eval harness. - The initial quant profiles are conservative; ops can opt into more aggressive profiles via tenant override in the Console. - There's an outstanding UX follow-up to display the safety lattice decisions in the Console trace view (tracked ENG-3578).

Migration & ops notes: To enable globally, set infra/helm/values-prefill.yaml -> enable_prefill_curator: true and provide sku_overrides for critical SKUs. For Private customers, include sample-tenant.yaml during installer-run to seed tenant defaults. The runbook provides rollback steps and queries to validate prefill hit rate and econ deltas before and after enabling.

Merge outcome: Merged via squash on 2025-11-21 after green CI and approvals from two reviewers.

Why this is different: Unlike prior PRs that focused on single knobs (batching or quant presets), this change ties SKU-awareness, tenant defaults, telemetry-based safeguards, and a small runtime safety lattice together so that quant and prefill defaults behave conservatively by default and can be tuned safely per-tenant.
